newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe aims for tourism boom in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe aims for tourism boom in 1997/98.

text.p: Zimbabwean tourism officials meet for two days starting on Wednesday to map out ways of bolstering an industry that has grown at an average 10 percent annually in the past five years.

Environment and Tourism deputy minister Edward Chindori- Chininga told state radio ahead of the annual congress of the Zimbabwe Council for Tourism (ZCT) in Bulawayo that there was still great scope in developing the industry which contributes about five percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
"We have to look at all aspects and see where and how we can enhance our products, and then ensure we market ourselves aggressively," he said.
"We must find a way of supporting the boom that we expect this year and even in 1998," he added.

The ZCT has been urging tourism industry operators in Zimbabwe -- whose tourism attractions include the famous Victoria Falls in the north -- to market their products jointly with others in southern Africa.
President Robert Mugabe's government introduced a two percent tourism levy last July aimed at promoting Zimbabwe as a tourist destination.
Zimbabwe is estimated to have earned Z$1.63 billion (U.S.$150 million) in 1996 from tourism, up from Z$1.34 billion (U.S.$123 million) in 1995.

But a World Bank study says foreign visitors spent Z$1.9 billion in 1995, as much as three times in real terms as in 1990, arguing that the official figures from tourism do not take into account incidental spendings.

Chindori-Chininga estimates employment in all tourism-related businesses rose to about 100,000 in 1996 from 85,000 the previous year, and with more development could add some 20,000 more job openings this year.
Industry officials say some 1.4 million tourists visited the country -- mainly from neighbouring South Africa -- in 1996 and the number may rise to 1.6 million this year.
